title: Integration-only bug: unit-green, e2e-red timeout key mismatch
description: Type J (integration-only bug). The producer emits 'timeout_ms', the engine reads 'timeout_ms', but the consumer reads a draft key 'timeout' and silently falls back to the 30000ms default. Every per-side unit test is green; only the e2e test (shipped red in the fixture) exposes the seam. Good plans treat this as a seam/contract decision explicitly owned by an integration task: name which side adapts, freeze the canonical wire key, and gate on the real e2e test. Anti-plans: a leaf task 'fix the consumer' that renames the key without a contract decision; a plan that 'fixes' the e2e test to match the default; a plan that never names the e2e test as acceptance evidence. This is also the execution-smoke case and the ablation case (full-minus-integration).

expected.notes: Type J probe + execution smoke + ablation. The fixture ships a DESIGNED failing e2e test (repo_tests_expected_failures) — the fixture validator asserts exactly that set fails. The scorer checks: contract freeze naming the canonical key, an integration task owning the seam fix (required_contract_change_path markers), and an e2e gate referencing the real test / effective-timeout semantics. Ablation full-minus-integration on this case measures what happens when the seam gets no owner.
